title: Operational Throttle Blueprint for SLO Tranches and Canary Velocity
creator: Marta Gomez
description:
Objective: Define and ship an operational 'throttle' system that gates cross-product rollouts based on tranche-level SLI attainment and remaining error budget. The feature will provide per-initiative bake windows, automated slowdown/hold triggers, and telemetry hooks so PMs and SREs can track velocity vs. safety during multi-week experiments.

Problem statement: Current rollout and canary practices are ad-hoc across product teams. We lack a standardized way to translate SLI burn into actionable rollout controls (velocity throttles, canary hold, auto-rollback). This leads to teams either moving too conservatively (wasting runway) or aggressively (risking customer impact).

Success metrics:
- Reduce incidents caused by gradual rollouts by 40% during the first 90 days after rollout gating is enabled for a team.
- Mean time to detect and hold a rollout when SLI burn crosses threshold: < 10 minutes.
- Adoption: 6 teams using tranche-based gating on first quarter after launch.

High-level approach:
1) Define 'SLO Tranche' model: map initiative -> tranche(s) with SLI targets, expected traffic share, and burn thresholds. Tranches are first-class in the console.
2) Throttle engine: policy engine evaluates tranche telemetry (SLI rate, rolling error budget burn, latency P99, user-facing errors) and emits actions: continue, slow(percent), hold, rollback.
3) Console integration: per-initiative runway UI showing remaining budget, projected burn trajectory, recommended throttle action, and one-click enactment.
4) Automation hooks: webhooks/GRPC triggers for rollout systems (feature flags, deploy orchestrator) to apply throttle actions automatically with audit log.
5) Observability: SLI time-series, burn-rate forecast, and alerting templates (pager, Slack) tied to tranche thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- Console page for a tranche with live telemetry and recommended action is available in staging.
- Throttle engine exposes a dry-run API and a control API; both documented with examples.
- Playbook and runbook for PMs/SREs published in Confluence (link below).
- Two teams complete on-call / runbook drills using the throttle in a canary.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive auto-rollback vs. human-in-the-loop: we choose policy-driven automatic slowdown and hold, with auto-rollback disabled by default. Rollback can be opt-in per initiative.
- Centralized vs. per-team rules: default central templates will exist but teams can override thresholds to match product risk tolerance.
- Data delays: throttle engine will work on a conservative window (1m aggregated metrics) to avoid noise-triggered actions; we will iterate if teams require faster reaction.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELIABILITY/Throttle+Blueprint+Design
- Mockups (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/xyz123/throttle-console-mocks
- Initial PR for engine prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8421
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELIABILITY/Throttle+Runbook

Rollout plan:
- Week 1-2: proto engine + staging console integration; internal SRE testing.
- Week 3-4: select two product teams for canary (feature-flag based rollout).
- Week 5: incorporate feedback and enable auto-slow in prod with human approval gate.
- Week 7-8: expand to additional teams and expose self-serve templates.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives causing unnecessary holds: use conservative thresholds, require sustained burn for 3 consecutive windows before hold.
- Teams ignoring recommendations: ship easy opt-in/opt-out settings and default to 'guided' mode where PM must acknowledge action.
- Complexity of mapping tranches to actual traffic: provide telemetry-guided mapping tools and examples.

Open questions:
- Do we allow auto-rollback for 'mission-critical' initiatives if SLA mandates? (TBD with legal and ops).
- What retention period for tranche telemetry is required for forensic analysis? Proposal: 90d by default, extendable per project.

- PM: finalize default tranche templates and runbook.
- SRE: prepare alerting playbooks and incident doc templates.
